newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilians vote in mayoral election runoffs.
newsitem.headline: Brazilians vote in mayoral election runoffs.

text.p: Voters in half of Brazil's cities and towns flocked to the polls on Friday morning in runoff municipal balloting with Sao Paulo, the country's largest city, poised to elect its first black mayor.
As second-round balloting began, right-wing candidate and political neophyte Celso Pitta of the PPB party held a commanding 22 percentage point lead over former mayor Luiza Erundina in Sao Paulo.
With Friday declared a nationwide holiday, many Brazilians went to the polls early to free up their day to begin enjoying the three-day weekend.
Early reports from around the country showed voting was running smoothly. As a precaution, troops were called out in three state capitals -- Maceio, Manaus and Natal.

As in first-round Oct. 3 balloting, voters punched candidates' numbers into shoe-box-sized electronic ballot boxes, this time without the snags that marred last month's vote, which was Latin America's first computerized election.
"The ballot boxes are working well," said voter Ruy Moraes Pinto. "People seem to be catching on."
After lengthy campaigns that focused on local issues of transport, health care and crime, the elections promised few surprises.

In Rio de Janeiro, pre-vote polls showed Luiz Paulo Conde of the rightest Liberal Front Party (PFL) held a hefty 17 percentage point lead over Sergio Cabral of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's Social Democratic Party (PSDB).
